definition: Protected Routes is a core concept in React Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Protected Routes is
theory.body: Protected Routes describes the methods and patterns used within React Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Protected Routes is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Protected Routes matters
theory.body: Without Protected Routes, systems built with React Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Protected Routes works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Protected Routes follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Protected Routes.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Protected Routes
theory.body: Protected Routes offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
